scope: Four sequential full-board commands, including all normal rendering and audits. Revision-to-revision comparison, NOT identical hardware inputs or a language-only benchmark.

environment.host: same local host for all runs

sampling: One sample each, order Python carrier, C++ carrier, C++ devkit, Python devkit. No concurrent agent builds/tests. OS caches and unrelated background activity uncontrolled. No source edits in baseline export.
baseline_preparation: git archive of the exact Python commit extracted into a fresh temporary directory; Python invoked with -B
cpp_commands: October 18 reproduction settings in docs/RELEASE-2026-10-16.md, prefixed with /usr/bin/time -p; default project output directories, no --no-render
render_workload: Both revisions request eight high-quality opaque 1600x1200 3D views and per-sheet renders. Other image and audit workloads are revision-dependent.

mandatory_failures: testpoints: 9/23 required covered, 5 waived in historical source
design_rules: 2 findings, 2 waived in historical source

current_validation: Both C++ commands passed mandatory gates and source audits. Advisory return_path, golden and contract_coverage_lint failures remain. Zero non-unrouted DRC errors; 499 carrier/408 devkit unrouted connections. Not fabrication readiness.
limitations: Hardware designs, placement strategies, audit implementations and coverage differ; not a matched-input speedup claim.
Historical phase spans overlap background PCB work and combine audits/rendering/generation. Do not subtract these spans to fabricate historical audit-free timings.
Current sheet stage combines KiCad checks and rendering; PCB model stage includes internal checks. No pure-generation total is established.
Compile time was not measured in these commands; a fresh clean compilation measurement remains outstanding.
Logs and isolated baseline are local ephemeral evidence; hashes and measured values are retained here.
